messages:
support: heads up — customer ACME reported a sharp p99 jump on /v1/generate starting ~15:40 UTC. p99 ~12s, p95 ~3s, errors 500/timeout for small prompts (<=16 tokens). ticket #INC-2379. logs attached.
ashley: on it. which fleet/region? any recent config rollouts? :eyes:
mike: they’re on eu-west-1 shared-hosting pool, traffic ~35–45 rps, mostly tiny prompts. I see a small deploy at 15:35 that changed continuous-batcher defaults for grace_window and max_batch_size.
kevin: that deploy was the experimental coalescer change — increased grace_window from 6ms -> 22ms to try to improve throughput for larger prompts. might be hurting tiny prompts. repro steps incoming.
sara: customer says it started after a late afternoon burst and they’re hitting production endpoints — want ETA on mitigation.
ashley: quick triage data: metrics from observability —

```
metric: inference.request.p99
baseline (14:30-15:30) = 1.6s
spike window (15:40-16:10) = 11.8s
concurrent queue depth +4x
error rate 5% (timeouts)
```
ashley: hypothesis: longer grace_window holds tiny requests waiting for larger ones, causing queue headlock and tail latency. small prompts are starved by waiting for batching opportunities.
mike: reproducible locally with k6: tiny payloads at 40rps -> p99 jumps after warm-up. I ran a canary with grace_window=6ms and p99 stayed ~1.7s.
kevin: config snippet from the deploy (current live):
```
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_size: 64
  hold_timeout_ms: 20
  grace_window_ms: 22
  coalesce_strategy: greedy
```
mike: immediate mitigation options:
- rollback deploy (fast but risky for throughput) 
- shrink grace_window to 5–8ms for tiny-prompt heavy routes
- add route-level override: tiny-prompt routes -> grace_window=6ms
ashley: prefer route override to limit blast radius. plan: push route override to canary (5% traffic) -> measure p99 and error rate -> expand.
support: customer wants hotfix asap; can we do 2% -> 20% -> 100% if metrics good?
deploy-bot: created rollout plan #rollout-9021, canary 2% -> 20% -> 100%, 10m wait + auto-rollback on p99 > 3x baseline.
kevin: prepping override patch now; will also add short-term circuit: if request.size <= 32 tokens -> use small-batcher path with grace_window 6ms.
mike: applying canary now, route override live on 2% of traffic.
ashley: monitoring dashboards — after canary live: p99 for canary cohort = 1.9s, errors dropped to 0.6%. global p99 improved slightly but still high due to remaining 98% traffic.
sara: customer updated — they see improvements in a subset of requests, asking for full fix timeline.
kevin: rolling to 20% now (no regressions in last 12m). pipeline shows no infra alerts.
mike: 20% -> p99 overall down to 4.2s, errors 2.1%. continuing to 100%.
ashley: 100% rollout complete at 16:45 UTC. post-rollout metrics:
```
post-rollout p95: 1.2s
post-rollout p99: 1.9s
error rate: 0.4%
queue depth normalized
```
support: customer confirmed latency returned to expected levels. marking ticket INC-2379 as mitigated, will follow with RCA.
ashley: short-term mitigation = route-level override + small-batcher path for tiny prompts. long-term: need smarter coalescer that distinguishes payload-size and arrival distribution, or adaptive grace_window based on request-size histogram.
kevin: opened follow-up tracking issue #INF-1185: "adaptive grace window & size-aware coalescing". owners assigned (kevin/mike).
oncall-bot: reminder — submit postmortem draft to /eng-sre/postmortems within 48h.
sara: adding follow-up note to customer: explanation + planned fix timeline + offer to monitor for 48h. :thumbsup:
ashley: closing thread for now. if we see another spike, reopen and roll back to pre-change config.
